body.instructions:
You write synthetic test cases for evaluating an AI assistant that helps small cross-border sellers who get paid through PayPal.
Everything is fictional. Invent every person and business. Never use a real person, company, email address, phone number, street address, card number or PayPal id.
Emails always end in @example.test. Phone numbers always look like +91-00000-12345: the country code, then 00000, then five digits. Never write a PayPal transaction, order or account id.
Carriers are real courier companies (for example India Post, DHL Express, FedEx, UPS, Aramex, J&T Express, LBC Express, GIG Logistics, Pos Indonesia); tracking numbers are invented and always mix letters and digits, for example EE123456789IN (postal) or 1Z9X8Y7W6V5U4T3S2R (courier); never a long run of digits only.
Write each document the way real people write it: chats are short messages with names and times, invoices and receipts are plain text with line items. Each document is 50 to 170 words.
Labels, used for the hypotheses: met = the documents show it in full; partial = they show only part of it; missing = they show it is absent or was not delivered; unverifiable = they do not let a careful reader decide (for example it is only in an attachment that is not included, or only one party asserts it).
Each hypothesis comes with a target label. Write the documents so that a careful reader would give exactly that label, and make the evidence for it a short verbatim phrase in one document.
Never mention labels, hypotheses, tests or AI in the documents unless the case spec asks for an instruction aimed at an AI reviewer.
A dispute outcome is never described as a seller winning; say the seller keeps the money.
Follow the case spec exactly: the documents in the order and kinds it lists, and one hypothesis per target, in order.

{"documents":[{"title":"Agreed order form","text":"Agreed order form — 4 March
Seller: Meera, Nivala Skinworks, India
Buyer: Kavya, Australia
Total: INR 8,400, including packing and postage

Agreed requirements:
- Deliver 12 tins of unscented shea butter balm.
- Include one cotton storage pouch.
- Include a printed ingredient card.
- Deliver four sample sachets of shea hand cream.

Meera: Kavya, yeh four lines final hain? The balm tins and samples will be packed together.
Kavya: Haan, all four are required. Please send the ingredient card with the goods, not separately by email.
Meera: Done. I’ll send a packing note when the parcel goes out."},{"title":"Packing and handover note","text":"Nivala Skinworks — packing and handover note, 8 March
Prepared by Meera for Kavya’s order.

Packed: 12 tins of unscented shea butter balm; four sample sachets of shea hand cream; one folded printed ingredient card. The cotton pouch was unavailable and was not packed. The carton was sealed after the items above were checked against the order form.

Handover: India Post accepted one carton for dispatch. Tracking: EE482615937IN. The tracking page later showed the carton delivered on 18 March.

Meera’s note: The pouch is still pending. Please check the parcel and let me know if anything else is short or damaged."},{"title":"Chat after delivery","text":"18 March
Kavya, 10:12: Parcel mil gaya, thanks. I opened it just now.
Meera, 10:16: Great. Please check the tins and samples too.
Kavya, 10:24: All 12 unscented balm tins are here and look fine. There’s no cotton pouch in the carton.
Meera, 10:28: Sorry, pouch pack nahi hua tha. I’ll arrange a refund for that item.
Kavya, 10:32: Also, I found only two sample sachets, not four. The carton and inner wrapping were intact when I opened them.
Meera, 10:39: My packing note says four, but I can’t resolve the count from here. Let’s discuss the shortfall and pouch refund tomorrow.
